newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse closes sharply higher on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse closes sharply higher on Thursday.

text.p: French shares closed sharply higher on Thursday, lifted by market friendly U.S. economic data and optimism that a European Union budget deficit control pact would be approved at an EU summit next week.
The CAC-40 index closed up 64.08 points, or 2.38 percent at 2,760.27 after trading higher all session.
CAC-40 June futures were at 2,744 against 2,688 at Thursdays close.
Total volume was a high 10.4 billion francs
Dealers said the breaking of the key technical resistance level of 2,750 paved the way for a quick rally to 2,800.

The markets were reassured on the euro, which was their number one worry. There is now a good chance that the stability pact will be signed with the addition of a clause on growth and employment," said Roland Cagnon, stocks strategist at CDC Bourse.
"In the medium term, the markets will continue to rise and we are maintaining our objective of 3,000 on the index in six months," he said.
Another dealer said the new government's actions on the stability pact and on the politically sensitive Renault plant closure at Vilvoorde had reassured the markets.
"Let's wait for the general policy speech" on June 19, he said. Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will address the National Assembly next Thursday and lay out his government's programme.

Renault was up 4.89 percent at 139.50 francs. The share has now more than made up the ground it lost in previous sessions due to worries about the new government's position on the company's plans to close its assembly plant in Belgium.
Carrefour closed up 3.54 percent at 4,177 francs boosted by foreign buyers. The share ended off its year high set earlier in the session of 4,210 francs.
Total up 0.18 percent at 554 francs. Salomon Brothers has turned negative for the short term because of the drop in crude oil prices.
Promodes ended up 1.43 percent at 2,130 francs. The company denied rumours in the market that it would issue convertible debt.
L'Oreal closed 3.72 percent higher at 2,344 francs after the annual general meeting which was held today. The company has predicted higher profits and sales in 1997.
